transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Hi. Yeah, thanks for seeing me. Um... well, I guess I'm here because things have just gotten really, really out of hand lately. It's hard to even say out loud, to be honest. I work at an auto shop—I'm a mechanic—and, well, it's a stressful environment, and sometimes I just... I end up eating so much. Just way, way too much. And the second I do, this massive panic sets in about the weight. I mean, I really panic about gaining weight, you know? I can't stand the thought of it, and it makes me feel so disgusted with myself. 

So, what I've been doing—and this is why I finally made the appointment, because it's just taking over my whole life now—I go into the bathroom, whether it's the crappy one at the shop or my own at home, and I make myself throw it all up. I just force myself to get sick so I don't put on the pounds. At first, it was just, I don't know, a quick fix if I felt like I overdid it, but now... I mean, I go in, I lock the door, I turn on the fan or run the water so nobody out in the bays hears me, and it's just this whole exhausting routine. And honestly, doctor, I'm terrified. I'm sitting there on the bathroom floor wiping my mouth, and I realize I can't stop. I literally can't stop doing it. It's like my brain just takes over and I have to get it out, and it's scaring the hell out of me.
How often do you find yourself making yourself vomit after eating to keep from gaining weight?

Well, it's... it's a lot. Honestly, it's been happening so much lately that I lose track of the exact number, but I can tell you that for at least the past three months, there’s hardly been a single week where I didn’t have one of those awful, out-of-control eating episodes and then immediately go make myself throw up afterward. 

It's usually late at night, you know? After a long shift at the shop, my hands are still stained with grease, my back is just screaming at me—I've got this chronic lower back thing from leaning over engines all day—and I just feel so drained. So I start eating, and then the panic hits, and I end up in the bathroom. Some weeks, it happens several times. Especially when my back is acting up and I'm stuck at home more, just sitting there with my thoughts and the food. It's like the more time I have on my hands, the worse it gets. I'll tell myself, "Okay, just this once, just to fix this one mistake," but then Tuesday turns into Thursday, and then it's the weekend, and I'm right back over the toilet. It's just this constant, exhausting cycle that I can't break out of, no matter how much I promise myself I will.
How many times a week would you say you’ve made yourself vomit after overeating, on average, over the past few months?

Well, if I really have to put a number on it... I mean, like I was saying, for at least the past three months, there’s hardly been a single week where I didn’t have one of those late-night eating episodes and then go make myself throw up afterward. But if you want an average... gosh, it's hard because it fluctuates, you know? But it's a lot. I'd say it's easily, on average, maybe eight, nine, sometimes ten times a week. 

Some weeks it happens several times a day, especially when I’m home more because of my back. Like last week, my sciatica was just flaring up so badly I couldn't even stand up straight under the lift at work, so I took a couple of days off. And being home, just sitting there in my recliner with the TV on, trying to distract myself from the pain... the food is just right there in the kitchen. I'd eat, panic, throw up, and then an hour later, the whole cycle would start again. It's like the physical pain in my back just triggers this emotional need to eat, and then the guilt hits, and I'm back in the bathroom. So yeah, it's definitely not just a once-a-week thing. It's almost every day, and sometimes multiple times a day when things are really bad. It's just so exhausting, you know? I wake up feeling dehydrated and my throat is always scratchy, and I just think, "How did I let this happen again?" But then the evening rolls around, the shop closes, I get home, and it's like I'm on autopilot.
